item.title: Beijing’s billion-barrel weapon: Why India must prepare for China-driven oil prices
item.description: China has accumulated as much as 1.4 billion barrels in strategic and enterprise-controlled inventories, according to a new RAND study. That is more than three times the roughly 413 million barrels held in the US government’s Strategic Petroleum Reserve.
item.dc:creator: SMRITI JAIN

item.title: ‘Fed up of wife’s affair’, Bengaluru man kills two daughters, attempts suicide
item.description: A father allegedly strangled his two young daughters to death in a Bengaluru hotel. He was later found unconscious with his throat slit, attempting suicide. Hotel staff discovered the tragic scene after receiving no response from the room. A death note found at the scene cited marital issues as the motive. The accused is currently undergoing treatment while police investigate the incident.
item.dc:creator: RAJIV KALKOD

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg's $300m yacht booed over rescue call; clarification issued
item.description: In a surprising turn of events, Mark Zuckerberg's opulent yacht, Launchpad, faced backlash for not helping a stranded vessel within reach. Crew members clarified that they were on a different radio frequency and claimed assistance was imminent. A cruise ship later intervened, safely bringing the disabled boat back to Farragut Bay. Passengers on the cruise ship expressed their discontent by booing the yacht, which was positioned nearer to the emergency.

item.description: Novelist MacKenzie Scott returns to fiction writing after a thirteen-year hiatus. She will serially release an eighty-thousand-word novel throughout the month of August. Her recent donation of twenty million dollars supports mental health initiatives.

item.title: Florida restores 55,000 acres after removing 260 miles of roads
item.description: The Picayune Strand Restoration Project in Southwest Florida has been completed after years of work to restore the natural flow of water across 55,000 acres of wetlands. The project removed more than 260 miles of roads and plugged almost 50 miles of canals. The work is expected to improve wetlands, water quality and wildlife habitat.

item.title: 87-lb paddlefish tagged in 2007 caught again at 98 lbs, 18 years later
item.description: An impressive paddlefish, initially tagged in 2007, made headlines when an angler recaught it after an astonishing eighteen years. This ancient species revealed invaluable long-term growth data to scientists, adding eleven pounds and increasing its length by three inches. Such recaptures are pivotal, offering critical insights into fish survival and migration, underscoring the necessity of sustained fish tagging initiatives for conservation efforts.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Google Drive ends Photos backups starting August 10: What users need to do
item.description: Starting August 10, 2026, the Google Drive desktop app will no longer support backups for Google Photos. Users are required to switch to the Google Photos app to continue folder backups smoothly. Thankfully, existing photos will remain intact and secure. However, to enable new automatic backups, users must adjust their settings, as this change affects only computer folder backups, leaving phone backups unaffected.

item.title: 39 weeks pregnant wife performs CPR for 15mins to save husband
item.description: A pregnant woman helped save her husband’s life after his heart suddenly stopped in the middle of the night, performing CPR for around 15 minutes while she was 39 weeks pregnant. Days later, their newborn daughter met her father while he was still in a coma, in an emotional moment the family described as “the craziest experience” of their lives.

item.title: For India, the Mecca pact is a setback. For China, it's a warning
item.description: A new defense pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey has been signed. This agreement is seen as a setback for India's regional interests. China may benefit commercially from increased weapon system access. However, the pact could also reduce US military focus in West Asia. This shift might allow greater US attention on China's growing influence.

item.description: Martina Navratilova has questioned the WNBA’s current eligibility wording after Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White announced plans to enter the 2027 draft. Cathy Engelbert says league leaders will discuss the issue next week. Navratilova has also backed Aryna Sabalenka and the WTA’s new one-time SRY gene testing rule. item.title: 97-year-old Betty Bromage breaks her own Guinness World Record as oldest wing walker
item.description: Betty Bromage, aged ninety-seven, has once again become the world's oldest female wing walker. She achieved this remarkable feat in Gloucestershire, United Kingdom on August fourth, 2026. This accomplishment came just a year after she suffered a stroke, proving age is no barrier. Bromage undertook the thrilling adventure to raise funds for the hospital that cared for her. Her actions highlight a growing trend of seniors embracing adventurous travel experiences.

item.title: 'You can laugh at solution': Sindhu reacts to monkey-proof Worlds preps
item.description: PV Sindhu praised organisers preparing Delhi’s BWF World Championships venue after animals disrupted the India Open earlier this year. The Indira Gandhi Stadium has been upgraded with sealed vents, double doors, anti-pest gel and predator-call machines. According to TimesofIndia.com, four men trained to imitate langur calls have also been hired to deter monkeys. Sindhu called the efforts uniquely Indian and warmly welcoming.

item.title: SpaceX retail investors sell $4.5 million in shares, first net outflow since IPO
item.description: Retail investors turned into net sellers of SpaceX shares as of August 7, marking the end of a buying frenzy. This change coincided with a stock price recovery, indicating that individuals may be taking profits. The shares have struggled post-IPO, dropping beneath the initial offering price. Investors who were hopeful at the launch might now be looking to reduce their losses, even amidst a slight recovery in recent days.

item.title: Ethanol-blended diesel fails safety test, says govt; wider use ruled out for now
item.description: Ethanol-blended diesel fails safety specifications, lowering its flash point significantly. Public sector oil companies tested these blends, finding them unsuitable for current use. India is expanding ethanol use in petrol and exploring it for cooking fuel. Oil marketing companies have already procured large volumes of ethanol for blending. Further decisions on petrol blending will follow scientific and technical studies.

item.description: The Pakistan Hockey Federation (PHF) announced the change just hours before the Pakistan squad left for the World Cup. Kruis, who had initially been appointed head coach, will instead work as an adviser to the federation, while Veldhof will take charge of the national team.

item.title: 7.4-magnitude quake kills 77 in Colombia; death toll 'could top 1,000'
item.description: A significant earthquake jolted western Colombia on Monday, resulting in injuries and extensive destruction. fourty seven fatalities have been confirmed while multiple buildings collapsed across the country. Air travel was halted at several airports in various cities. The quake's impact was felt as far as Bogota and neighboring nations, raising concerns about possible aftershocks. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella is actively overseeing emergency response and recovery efforts.
